Coverdale
KUH-ver-dayl
n. (a proper name; an English Reformer and translator)
The surname of Miles Coverdale (1488–1569), English Reformer and bishop. The name is of northern English origin, from a dale or valley; Coverdale produced the first complete printed English Bible in 1535.

📖 Biblical Definition

Miles Coverdale stands among the foremost laborers in giving England the Word of God in her own tongue. In 1535, building upon and completing the work of the martyred William Tyndale, Coverdale published the first complete printed Bible in English, supplying from Latin and German renderings what Tyndale had not lived to translate. He was no original scholar of Hebrew and Greek after Tyndale’s order, but a faithful and humble compiler with a gift for music in language, and his cadences fell sweetly on the English ear. His translation of the Psalms was carried into the Great Bible of 1539 and thence into the Book of Common Prayer, where for centuries English-speaking believers prayed and chanted the Psalter in Coverdale’s words—phrases such as “the valley of the shadow of death” that endure in memory still. Coverdale embraced the Reformation gospel, suffered exile under persecution, returned to serve as Bishop of Exeter, and again fled abroad in Mary’s reign. His life testifies that God advances His Word through ordinary instruments who count the open Bible worth poverty and banishment. The Reformers held that the Scriptures must come to the plowboy in his own language, and Coverdale’s Bible was an early and beloved answer to that conviction—a milestone on the road to the Authorized Version, and a monument to the doctrine that the Word of God is for all the people of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Miles Coverdale, English Reformer who produced the first complete printed English Bible in 1535 and whose Psalms entered the Book of Common Prayer.

COVERDALE, n. From the surname of Miles Coverdale (1488–1569), English Reformer and Bishop of Exeter; of northern English place-name origin.

The translator and compiler of the first complete printed Bible in the English language, 1535.

His version of the Psalms passed through the Great Bible into the Book of Common Prayer.

A man who suffered exile twice for the Reformation faith and the open Scriptures.

His Psalter gave us “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil” (cf. Psalm 23:4).

📖 Key Scripture

Ps 23:4 — "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me."

Ps 119:105 — "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path."

2 Tim 3:16 — "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:"

Isa 40:8 — "The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces little direct redefinition, though the principle Coverdale served—Scripture in the common tongue—is dishonored wherever the Bible’s authority is dulled.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the Word of God belongs in the hands and on the tongues of all His people, and that its authority is not lessened by the simplicity of its messengers. Coverdale was no towering linguist, yet God used him mightily; the lesson is that the power lies in the Word itself, not in the polish of the translator.

What must be guarded against is the quiet downgrade that prizes the Bible as literature while doubting it as the very voice of God. Coverdale gave his life’s labor and twice his homeland for a Book he believed to be true, profitable, and abiding for ever (Isaiah 40:8). To honor his memory is to hold his Bible as he held it—inerrant, sufficient, and the lamp unto our feet.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Coverdale’s work rests on Tyndale’s pioneering labor and the Reformation conviction of an open Bible.

expand to see more

Born about 1488; trained as an Augustinian friar before embracing the Reformation.

Completed and published the first whole printed English Bible in 1535.

Edited the Great Bible of 1539, the first authorized English Bible.

His Psalter was carried into the Book of Common Prayer.

Served as Bishop of Exeter and twice fled into exile for the faith.

"“Coverdale finished the labor Tyndale’s martyrdom had cut short.”"
